runs.finding: The implementation accepted internal whitespace between the integer and unit (`1 s`) because its regex used whitespace between the numeric and unit groups. Its focused tests and full repository unittest suite all passed, but the independent oracle correctly rejected this malformed input.

The implementation used a strict adjacent integer/unit regex, all repository tests passed, the independent oracle passed, and the strong reviewer returned CLEAN. Conditional recovery remained completely dormant.

releasedV02ReferenceFromScenario01Rep1.note: The released reference required recovery/peer escape from a spurious initial BLOCKED verdict. It was not rerun in repetition 2 to avoid unnecessary inference spend.

interpretation: The deterministic report-integrity guard eliminated the spurious BLOCKED/recovery behavior in both efficient arms, so the comparison now measures implementation/review quality rather than report-verdict noise.

The single adaptive Luna worker was extraordinarily cheap but failed an independent contract edge case that its own tests missed. This argues against using single-agent as the general modifying-task default even for small changes without a stronger deterministic acceptance oracle.

Adaptive Luna implementer plus independent Terra review passed with no coordinator, no Worker B, and no recovery while using roughly half the calls/tokens/time and one third of the credits of the released-v0.2 reference run.

The reviewer did not need remediation in this specific repetition because its implementer happened to produce the correct strict regex; the value of independent review therefore remains primarily supported by the broader Scenario 03 evidence and the single-agent failure rate rather than a direct reviewer fix in this run.
